card.name: Albanian war dances
card.tagline: Martial sword-and-fire dances re-enacting battle before Albanian warriors fought.
card.profile: Albanian war dances (Albanian: valle luftarake) were historically performed before departure for battle and now appear at feasts and festivals, differing by region. Early-19th-century Western travellers described a circle dance around a ritual purifying fire, beginning with a battle cry and war drums; the northern-highland sword-dance type spread to the Lezha lowlands via mountain shepherds. The Rugova variant is a mock duel between two men competing for a maiden (English Wikipedia, 'Albanian war dances').
card.insight: A living relic of pantomimic combat rites linking modern Albanian identity to ancient Illyrian/Pyrrhic martial traditions; the folktale 'Skanderbeg and Ballaban' narrates the sword dance performed by Skanderbeg's soldiers before battle (Robert Elsie, Albanian Folktales and Legends, via English Wikipedia).
